Colorado CS-060 Substance Testing: notification-to-collection time lapse must be no more than 2 hours for residential clients and no more than 16 hours for non-residential clients, with notification documented.
Chain of custody and sample testing must meet acceptable evidentiary standards; urinalysis samples stored per standard practices.

In-house testing equipment (including breath testing) must operate per manufacturer guidelines with operator certification documented in personnel files; drug screening kits must meet FDA standards and be used per manufacturer instructions.

Per Colorado CS-061, an entry urine sample must be taken within 12 hours of admission, tested for cocaine metabolite, THC, amphetamines, opiates, barbiturates, benzodiazepine, alcohol, and creatinine levels; drug screening kits may not be used for entry samples, though private clinical labs or in-house testing equipment may be used.

Entry alcohol testing can be done via urinalysis and/or breathalyzer; entrance UA not required if a client changes service types within the same facility during a continuous residential stay or transfers residential to non-residential.
Per CS-062, testing frequency is assessed using the SSI-R, LSI, and entry UA results; until assessed, clients are treated as high risk and tested once per week.

Negative assessment for substance involvement = SSI-R score of 3 or less AND no risk indicated by LSI/collateral AND negative entry UA; positive = SSI-R of 4 or greater OR risk indicated OR positive entry UA.

Non-substance-involved clients are tested from once/month (residential levels 1-5, non-res level 6) to quarterly (levels 7-8); substance-involved clients range 4-8x/month at lower levels down to 1x per 2 months at level 8, with a maximum of 8x/month for all levels and at least one full polysubstance test per month.
Dilute UAs are treated as positive; all UA results must be returned within 3 business days; testing must be unexpected, unannounced, and unanticipated; recommended not to exceed 2x/week.

Per CS-063, unless the client admits use, positive results used to raise custody level must be confirmed by an outside lab using GC/MS and/or LC/MS/MS, with confirmatory results or a signed admission-of-use form kept in the case file.

Urinalysis collection must be visually monitored by staff of the same gender (case-by-case for transgender/intersex per PREA); outside labs must be properly licensed/certified; clients cannot be charged a fee for substance testing without written OCC approval; testing documentation (date/time, substances, staff/client ID, results) kept in individual case records.
Sanitary practices at testing site: no smoking, eating, or drinking; gloves used when handling samples; no food/medications stored near samples or test chemicals.

Dubois County Community Corrections (DCCC) offers nonclinical CBT-serviced programs including Staying Quit (SQ), a 12-week cognitive restructuring program that helps clients avoid relapse by recognizing risky situations, coping with urges and cravings, being around users, understanding support issues, and taking charge, targeted at Moderate and High/Very High-Risk clients.

Coping with Anger (Men and Women) is a 12-week cognitive restructuring and social skills program used as a supplemental program with domestic violence perpetrators, road rage, substance abuse, and drug courts.

MRT-Breaking the Chains of Trauma (Men and Women) is a 12-week cognitive restructuring program for recovering from trauma without reliving the experience, available in male, female, and Spanish workbooks.
Seeking Safety (Men and Women) is a 24-week evidence-based, present-focused counseling model to help people attain safety from trauma and/or addiction.

DCCC requires individual assessments including the Texas Christian University Criminal Thinking Scales (TCU CTS), given as a pretest at DCCC Orientation and again as a post-test when participants finish all required CBT classes.

Colorado Community Corrections Standards (CS-040) list acceptable monitoring methods: personal contact; staff-initiated monitors via active GPS-enabled ankle monitors; staff-initiated monitors via active GPS-enabled cellular phones including voice verification; verifiable documents issued by authorities (with legible date/time); and staff-initiated telephone contact with client, supervisor, treatment provider, or approved person.

All monitoring documentation shall include the monitoring method, time, date, client location, staff signature, and verification results; weekly and monthly monitors shall include a random combination of work and pass verifications.

Locations such as church, treatment, or movie theaters may be considered unverifiable; higher-level clients are generally expected to spend more time in pro-social community activities, some unverifiable.
Negative monitors require continued documented efforts to contact the client until whereabouts are determined or escape procedures initiated.

CS-042 Job Search: clients out for job search must be monitored at least twice per week; acceptable methods include personal contact, telephone contact with a potential employer, verifiable correspondence with partner agencies, GPS-enabled ankle monitor monitors, and active GPS cell phone monitors with voice verification.

CS-041 Furlough: privilege furloughs available on residential levels 3 and 4 (up to one 24-hour furlough/week on level 3, up to 48 hours/week on level 4), monitored twice per 24-hour period; emergency furlough monitor frequency ranges from every 12 hours (Level 1) to every 24 hours (Level 4), randomized and spaced.

CS-044 Home Visits/Community Contacts required for all non-residential clients; staff must physically enter the home before transition and during home visits check for stability and functioning; frequency ranges from 1/month (high risk, Levels 5-6) to 1/quarter or 2/year depending on risk and level; community contacts cannot be conducted consecutively.

CS-050: a log for each residential client records all authorized absences including client name, date, departure/return times, destination street address, purpose (work, pass, furlough, job search), and client acknowledgement (electronic/biometric permitted).

CS-043 Off-Grounds Surveillance: programs must have policies for staff contact with clients off grounds; staff generally have a duty to report but should be discouraged from confronting clients directly.
